walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report — a core area of Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: At the 0.05 significance level, what does a significant result mean?
options: There is less than a 5% probability the pattern arose by chance
The result is 95% wrong
The data contain no errors
The sample was 5% of the population

mcqs.q: Which measure describes the spread of data around the mean?
options: Standard deviation
Mode
Median
Mean

mcqs.q: Random, systematic and stratified are types of what?
options: Sampling strategy
Statistical test
Map projection
Graph

mcqs.q: Why pilot your data-collection methods before the main survey?
options: To find problems and improve reliability before committing time
To obtain the final results without checks
Because drones are compulsory in fieldwork
To avoid writing a methodology section

mcqs.q: Can the fieldwork report be written entirely from internet sources?
options: Correlation means the data were collected correctly.
Secondary data means data collected in the afternoon.
No - the internal assessment centres on primary data you collect in the field, although secondary sources can add context and comparison.
Good online research can replace collecting your own field data.

mcqs.q: Is an anomaly in your results a mistake you should delete?
options: Not necessarily - anomalies may be genuine and worth explaining; data should only be discarded with a clear methodological justification.
All anomalous points are errors and should be removed before analysis.
A single anomaly makes the whole report fail.
Secondary data means data collected in the afternoon.

mcqs.q: Does a correlation found in your field data prove causation?
options: Correlation means the data were collected correctly.
No - your analysis can show association, but claiming causation requires supporting theory and acknowledgement of other possible factors.
Secondary data means data collected in the afternoon.
If two variables I measured rise together, one must cause the other.

Use sampling (random/systematic) to gather data in the field
Organise into tables, graphs and maps (e.g. choropleth)
Apply tests like Spearman's Rank to find relationships
Answer the hypothesis using the evidence gathered
Assess reliability, limitations and how to improve the study
